# BPCS Interlock Record: Template and Worked Example

The design rests on three rules that keep setpoints in one place:

1. **One Interlock Setpoint Register for each unit.** It is the only document that holds trip values, delays, deadbands and bypass timers. Each value has an ID (`SP-<IL-ID>-NN`).
2. **Interlock records and FAT steps hold no numbers.** They cite SP-IDs only. The configurer enters values from the register. The FAT tester records the register revision used and the value found in the configuration.
3. **Alarm limits stay in the ISA-18.2 alarm database.** The register does not copy them. The register holds one rule: each pre-alarm must sit above or below its trip, as the case needs.

Legacy values go in a column of the register, not in the record. The comparison between old and new is then also kept in one place.

---

## Part 1: Interlock Register (one per unit)

This is the index for each unit. It lists every BPCS interlock in the unit.

| IL-ID | Unit | Description | Cause tag(s) | Effect tag(s) | Latched | SIS/BMS overlap checked (Y/N, ref) | Legacy source | Record rev | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Part 2: Interlock Setpoint Register (one per unit)

| SP-ID | IL-ID | Tag | Parameter | Value | Units | Legacy value (as found) | Legacy source | Basis / source | Status (Proposed / Confirm / Approved) | Rev |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Rule: if the new value differs from the legacy value, write the reason in "Basis / source". Process engineering approves the change through MOC if construction has started.

---

## Part 3: Interlock Record Template

```
INTERLOCK RECORD   IL-<ID>        Rev <n>      Unit <nnnn>
Equipment: <tag>   P&ID: <dwg/sheet>   C&E: <dwg/row or "this record">
```

**1. Purpose**
- What the interlock protects, in one STE sentence.
- The hazard or equipment damage that it prevents.

**2. Classification**
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Layer | BPCS (not SIS) |
| SIS/BMS function on same hazard | SIF ID and SRS ref, or "None" |
| Credited as IPL in LOPA | Y / N, with LOPA ref. If Y, the record must also meet the IPL independence requirements. |
| Independence from the initiating cause | The controller, I/O card and sensor are or are not shared with the control loop. |

**3. Causes**
| Cause ID | Tag | Condition | Trip SP-ID | Delay SP-ID | Voting | Reset/deadband SP-ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**4. Effects**
| Effect ID | Tag | Action on trip | Fail position (power/air/comms loss) | Confirmation feedback | Travel-time SP-ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

**5. Latching and reset**
- Latched or auto-reset.
- Reset permissives (all must be true).
- Reset method (HMI button, role, field reset).
- What reset does NOT do. For example: "Reset does not open the valve."

**6. Startup bypass** (only if the cause is healthy only after startup)
- The trigger, the timer SP-ID, and how the bypass ends automatically.

**7. Maintenance bypass**
- Who can apply it (role), how it is authorized, the maximum duration SP-ID, the alarm while active, and the log entry.

**8. Abnormal conditions**
| Condition | Response | Latched |
|---|---|---|
| Bad PV (out of range, fault, I/O bad quality) | | |
| Controller-to-I/O comms loss | | |
| HMI/server comms loss | | |
| Controller power loss / restart | | |
| Effect fails to reach position | | |

**9. Alarms** (reference the alarm database ID; if no database exists yet, list them here)
| Alarm ID | Tag | Type | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|---|

**10. Operator interface**
- What the faceplate shows, what the operator can change, and the prompts.

**11. Requirements**
| Req ID | Requirement (STE) | Test method (FAT / SAT / Inspection) | FAT step |
|---|---|---|---|

**12. FAT test steps**
| Step | Action | Expected result | SP-ID used | Recorded value | Pass/Fail |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

The tester records the register revision at the top of the test sheet.

**13. Migration traceability**
| Item | Legacy source (printout/drawing, sheet, rung) | Matches new record (Y/N) | Discrepancy ID |
|---|---|---|---|

**14. Open items**
| OI | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|

**15. Sign-off**
- Process engineering, controls engineering, operations (states, bypass, prompts), and the configurer.

---

## Part 4: Worked Example: IL-1105, Heater Low Fuel Gas Pressure

```
INTERLOCK RECORD   IL-1105        Rev A (draft)      Unit 11xx
Equipment: H-1101 (confirm heater tag)   P&ID: TBD   C&E: this record
```

### 1. Purpose
IL-1105 closes XV-1106 when PT-1105 shows low fuel gas pressure. Low fuel gas pressure can cause an unstable flame or a flameout at the burners of H-1101. IL-1105 isolates the main fuel before this occurs.

### 2. Classification
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Layer | BPCS |
| SIS/BMS function on same hazard | Most heater BMS designs also have a low-low fuel gas trip. Its reference is to be confirmed (OI-1). IL-1105 does not replace it. |
| Credited as IPL | Assumed N. To be confirmed against the LOPA (OI-1). |
| Independence | PT-1105 may also be the PV of the fuel gas pressure loop. To be confirmed (OI-2). |

### 3. Causes
| Cause ID | Tag | Condition | Trip SP-ID | Delay SP-ID | Voting | Reset SP-ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PT-1105 | PV below trip value for the full delay | SP-1105-01 | SP-1105-02 | 1oo1 | SP-1105-03 |
| C2 | PT-1105 | PV quality bad for the full delay | n/a | SP-1105-04 | 1oo1 | n/a |
| C3 | XV-1106 (maintenance bypass) | None. The bypass inhibits C1 and C2 only. See section 7. | n/a | n/a | n/a | n/a |

### 4. Effects
| Effect ID | Tag | Action on trip | Fail position | Feedback | Travel SP-ID |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | XV-1106 | De-energize the solenoid. The valve closes. | Closed (spring return, de-energize to trip) | ZSC-1106 / ZSO-1106 (confirm tags, OI-3) | SP-1105-05 |
| E2 | PIC-1105 (fuel gas pressure controller, confirm tag, OI-3) | Go to MAN. Set the output to the closed position. | Per the control valve datasheet | Controller mode | n/a |

E2 prevents a surge of fuel when the operator opens XV-1106 again.

### 5. Latching and reset
- IL-1105 is latched.
- Reset permissives (all true):
  - PT-1105 PV is above the reset value SP-1105-03.
  - PT-1105 quality is good.
  - ZSC-1106 shows closed.
- Reset method: a RESET button on the IL-1105 faceplate, available to the console operator role.
- Reset does not open XV-1106. The operator must give a separate OPEN command.
- Reset does not bypass a BMS purge or a light-off sequence.

### 6. Startup bypass
None, if PT-1105 is upstream of XV-1106 on the supply header. In that case, pressure is present before XV-1106 opens.

If PT-1105 is downstream of XV-1106, add a startup bypass:
- It starts when the operator opens XV-1106.
- It ends automatically after timer SP-1105-07.

See OI-4.

### 7. Maintenance bypass
- **Authorization:** the shift supervisor role applies the bypass with a bypass permit number.
- **Scope:** the bypass inhibits C1 and C2 only.
- **Duration:** the bypass removes itself at the maximum duration SP-1105-06.
- **Alarm and log:** ALM-1105-04 is active for the full bypass period. The log records the start, end, user and permit number.

### 8. Abnormal conditions
| Condition | Response | Latched |
|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 bad PV | Trip after SP-1105-04 (C2). Alarm ALM-1105-03. | Yes |
| Controller-to-I/O comms loss | The output card fails de-energized. XV-1106 closes. | Yes (IL-1105 starts tripped on recovery) |
| HMI/server comms loss | The logic continues in the controller. There is no change to XV-1106. | n/a |
| Controller power loss | XV-1106 closes (de-energized). | n/a |
| Controller restart | IL-1105 starts in the tripped state. XV-1106 stays closed until a reset and an OPEN command. | Yes |
| XV-1106 not closed at the end of SP-1105-05 | Alarm ALM-1105-05. | Alarm latched until acknowledged and ZSC-1106 shows closed |

### 9. Alarms
There is no alarm database reference yet. Move these alarms into the rationalized database (OI-5).

| Alarm ID | Tag | Type | Priority (proposed) | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ALM-1105-01 | PT-1105 | Low pre-alarm (limit in the alarm database, above SP-1105-01) | High | Find the cause of low supply pressure. Reduce the firing rate. |
| ALM-1105-02 | IL-1105 | Interlock tripped | Urgent | Make sure that XV-1106 is closed. Follow the heater trip procedure. |
| ALM-1105-03 | PT-1105 | Bad PV | High | Tell instrument maintenance. Do not reset until the PV is good. |
| ALM-1105-04 | IL-1105 | Bypass active | Low | Make sure that the bypass permit is valid. |
| ALM-1105-05 | XV-1106 | Failed to close | Urgent | Isolate the fuel gas manually at the local isolation valve. |

### 10. Operator interface
The IL-1105 faceplate shows:
- PT-1105 PV and quality.
- The trip value and reset value, read only, from the register.
- The trip state and the first-out cause (C1 or C2).
- The XV-1106 position.
- The bypass state and the time remaining.

The operator can:
- Push RESET.
- Command XV-1106 OPEN or CLOSE. OPEN is blocked while IL-1105 is tripped.

The operator cannot change trip values from the HMI.

Prompt after a reset: "IL-1105 reset. XV-1106 stays closed. Open XV-1106 only through the heater light-off procedure."

### 11. Requirements
| Req ID | Requirement | Test method | FAT step |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-IL1105-001 | When PT-1105 stays below SP-1105-01 for SP-1105-02, the BPCS closes XV-1106. | FAT | 2–4 |
| FR-IL1105-002 | When PT-1105 recovers before the end of SP-1105-02, IL-1105 does not trip. | FAT | 3 |
| FR-IL1105-003 | On trip, the BPCS sets PIC-1105 to MAN with the output closed. | FAT | 4 |
| FR-IL1105-004 | IL-1105 stays tripped until all reset permissives are true and the operator pushes RESET. | FAT | 5–6 |
| FR-IL1105-005 | RESET does not open XV-1106. | FAT | 6 |
| FR-IL1105-006 | When PT-1105 quality is bad for SP-1105-04, IL-1105 trips. | FAT | 7 |
| FR-IL1105-007 | The maintenance bypass inhibits C1 and C2, shows ALM-1105-04, and ends at SP-1105-06. | FAT | 8–9 |
| FR-IL1105-008 | After a controller restart, IL-1105 starts tripped and XV-1106 stays closed. | FAT | 10 |
| FR-IL1105-009 | If ZSC-1106 does not show closed within SP-1105-05 after a trip, the BPCS raises ALM-1105-05. | FAT | 11 |
| FR-IL1105-010 | The configured values agree with the register revision used for the test. | Inspection (FAT) | 1 |

### 12. FAT test steps
Before the test, write the setpoint register revision on the test sheet.

| Step | Action | Expected result | SP-ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Compare the configured trip, reset, delay and timer values with the register. | All values agree. | 01–07 |
| 2 | Simulate PT-1105 above SP-1105-03. Reset IL-1105. Open XV-1106. | XV-1106 opens. No alarms. | 03 |
| 3 | Set PT-1105 below SP-1105-01. Return it above SP-1105-01 before the end of SP-1105-02. | No trip. | 01, 02 |
| 4 | Set PT-1105 below SP-1105-01 for longer than SP-1105-02. | XV-1106 closes. PIC-1105 goes to MAN with the output closed. ALM-1105-02 shows. C1 is first out. | 01, 02 |
| 5 | Set PT-1105 between SP-1105-01 and SP-1105-03. Push RESET. | Reset is rejected. | 01, 03 |
| 6 | Set PT-1105 above SP-1105-03. Push RESET. | IL-1105 resets. XV-1106 stays closed. The prompt shows. | 03 |
| 7 | Simulate PT-1105 bad quality for longer than SP-1105-04. | Trip. C2 is first out. ALM-1105-03 shows. | 04 |
| 8 | Apply the maintenance bypass. Repeat step 4. | No trip. ALM-1105-04 shows. | 06 |
| 9 | Wait for the end of SP-1105-06 (accelerated timer allowed, note it on the sheet). | The bypass ends automatically. ALM-1105-04 clears. | 06 |
| 10 | Reset and open XV-1106. Stop and restart the controller. | IL-1105 starts tripped. XV-1106 is closed. | n/a |
| 11 | Simulate ZSC-1106 stuck off. Trip IL-1105. | ALM-1105-05 shows after SP-1105-05. | 05 |

### 13. Migration traceability
| Item | Legacy source | Matches | Discrepancy ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| Trip value | Legacy logic printout, sheet/rung TBD | TBD | — |
| Latching/reset | Legacy C&E drawing TBD | TBD | — |
| PIC-1105 to MAN on trip | Not known whether the legacy logic does this | TBD | OI-6 |

### 14. Open items
| OI | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-1 | Confirm the BMS/SIS low-low fuel gas SIF reference. Confirm that IL-1105 is not credited as an IPL. | Process safety | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-2 | Confirm whether PT-1105 is shared with the PIC-1105 loop. | Controls lead | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-3 | Confirm the H-1101, PIC-1105, ZSC-1106 and ZSO-1106 tags against the instrument index. | Controls lead | 2026-10-30 |
| OI-4 | Confirm the PT-1105 location relative to XV-1106 (decides the startup bypass). | Process engineering | 2026-10-30 |
| OI-5 | Move the ALM-1105 alarms into the rationalized alarm database. | Alarm management lead | 2026-11-20 |
| OI-6 | Get the legacy trip value and logic for IL-1105 from the printouts. Record them in the register. | Migration team | 2026-10-30 |
| OI-7 | Confirm the trip value SP-1105-01 against the burner datasheet. | Process engineering / burner vendor | 2026-11-13 |

### Setpoint register entries for IL-1105
| SP-ID | Tag | Parameter | Value | Units | Legacy value | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-1105-01 | PT-1105 | Low trip value | TBD (burner-specific, OI-7) | psig | TBD (OI-6) | Open |
| SP-1105-02 | PT-1105 | Trip delay | 2 | s | TBD | Proposed – confirm |
| SP-1105-03 | PT-1105 | Reset value (trip + deadband) | SP-1105-01 + 5 % of span | psig | TBD | Proposed – confirm |
| SP-1105-04 | PT-1105 | Bad PV trip delay | 2 | s | TBD | Proposed – confirm |
| SP-1105-05 | XV-1106 | Close travel time limit | 10 | s | TBD | Proposed – confirm against the valve datasheet |
| SP-1105-06 | IL-1105 | Maximum maintenance bypass | 8 | h | TBD | Proposed – confirm (operations) |
| SP-1105-07 | IL-1105 | Startup bypass timer (only if OI-4 requires it) | 30 | s | TBD | Proposed – confirm |

I left SP-1105-01 as TBD on purpose. A low fuel gas trip value depends on the burner. Use a number from the legacy logic and the burner datasheet, not one I propose.

---

## Notes for the 40-unit rollout

- **Keep the register as a database or a controlled spreadsheet, not as Word tables.** You can then export it and compare it automatically with the new DCS configuration. This also covers FAT step 1 for all units at once.
- **Log every disagreement between a legacy printout and a C&E drawing.** Give each one a discrepancy ID and resolve it before the record reaches Rev 0. Treat the running logic as "as-is" and the drawing as "as-intended" until process engineering decides.
- **Screen every heater, furnace and boiler interlock against the BMS/SIS scope before you write the record.** Fuel-related trips are the most likely to sit in both systems.
